description:
https://www.signumhq.com/app - FREE market intel on iOS and Android.

Bonds are supposed to rise when stocks fall. That is the entire premise of a 60/40 portfolio. We checked whether it is still true.

Every session from January 2015 to August 2026: 2,924 trading days. We pulled out every day the S&P fell 1% or more - 328 of them - and counted how often long Treasuries (TLT) closed higher.

On any random day, TLT rises 50.5% of the time.
On a hard down day for stocks, TLT rose 62.2% of the time.
That gap is real - a two-proportion z of 4.00.

So the textbook looks right. Until you split it by era:

2015-2019: bonds protected on 78.8% of crash days
2020-2021: 72.7%
2022-2026: 46.8%

46.8% is lower than the 50.5% you get on a random day. For the last four years, long Treasuries have been slightly LESS likely to rise on a stock crash day than on an ordinary one.

The ten-year average hides it completely. That is why nobody mentions it.

Data: SPY, TLT and IEF daily closes, 2015-01-01 to 2026-08-20. Counts and tests are ours.
Educational only. Not investment advice.

#bonds #investing #stockmarket
pinnedComment:
The full count, so you can check it:

- Window: 2015-01-01 to 2026-08-20, 2,924 sessions
- Hard down day = S&P (SPY) -1% or worse -> 328 days
- TLT rose on 50.5% of all days, 62.2% of hard down days (z = 4.00)

By era, on hard down days:
- 2015-2019: 78.8% (104 days)
- 2020-2021: 72.7% (66 days)
- 2022-2026: 46.8% (158 days) <- below the 50.5% baseline

IEF (intermediate Treasuries) tells the same story: 82.7% -> 71.2% -> 43.7%.
